**Asia pre-market reactions — 2026-11-04**

- Post-close scan of the just-finished Asian equity session (JP / TW / HK / KR), built 06:30 ET ahead of the US pre-open.
- All prices are the **settled close** of each market's 4 Nov session; market caps converted to USD at open.er-api rates (JPY 158.399, TWD 32.771, HKD 7.846, KRW 1,343.93).

**TL;DR**

- A **V-shaped election day**: early US-midterm results pointing to a Democratic Congress triggered an AI/data-centre-capex scare that hit Japan hardest, then both Japan and Korea round-tripped into the close.
- **Japan was the outlier** —
- Nikkei -1.42% to 62,188.63 after being as low as 60,030 (-4.7% intraday), with the damage concentrated in AI hardware/materials (NTT -6.02%, Furukawa -6.19%, Sumitomo Electric -7.25%, Kyocera -7.40%).
- Korea closed **up** (KOSPI +0.62%) and Hong Kong was the session's winner (+1.67%) on gold and HK-local AI hardware.
- **Biggest movers**: Lingbao Gold (HK) +17.04%, Hanwha Solutions (KR) +18.64%, Krafton (KR) +16.55%, Kurita Water (JP) +15.06%, HLB (KR) -17.69% on an FDA classification setback.
- Kurita's +15% is the one headline move **without a sourced catalyst**.
- **Order of this brief:** grouped by country — **Japan, Korea, Taiwan, Hong Kong** —
- and within each country every row is sorted by the absolute size of the move, biggest first.
- **Earnings-cycle context**: outside the Q3 reporting window for JP/TW; HK reports semi-annually;
- Korea's window is late Oct, so the KR prints that dominate the tape (Hanwha Solutions 9 Nov, SKC) are just behind us.

- **Driver of the day:** early US-midterm vote count showed a Democratic lead, raising the odds of tighter regulation of data-centre and AI infrastructure spending.
- Japan (AI-hardware heavy) sold off, then reversed; Korea reversed to positive; Hong Kong rallied on its own themes (spot gold > US$4,000/oz, HK-listed AI hardware chain, innovative drugs).

- **Japan note:** 3 Nov (Culture Day) was a TSE holiday, so every Japan change below is measured against the **2 Nov** close. Korea and Taiwan traded normally on 3 Nov.

**Degradation / handling**

- **Regional-venue stale prints (JP):** 13 NAG/FSE/SAPSE rows dropped as non-primary listings; each was resolved against its TSE line before use (11 primary rows recovered, e.g.
- FSE:7011 -21.00% vs TSE:7011 -3.30%, NAG:4062 -26.89% vs TSE:4062 -0.10%). Publishing a regional row would have created three false >20% movers.
- **HK CNY counters:** 4 rows dropped by `currency != HKD` (Lenovo 80992, CR Beer 80291, SHKP 80016, BOCHK 82388) —
- they quote off the liquid HKD line at an implied ~0.854 rate on tiny volume. No HKD dual-ticker duplicates survived.
- **KR preferred shares:** 13 preferred lines dropped where the common line exists (e.g.
- Hanjin KAL pfd +22.44% vs common +5.19%; Hanwha Solutions 009835 +9.53% vs 009830 +18.64%) — otherwise one company counts twice.
- **Earnings-driven column:** catalyst attribution covers the top reaction per market plus every name covered by the same press reports (HK gold / AI-hardware / innovative-drug themes, KR battery complex);
- the rest are marked `—` rather than guessed.
- 6 web lookups were made in total (2 above the skill's 4-call cap, for the -17.69% HLB move and the HK AI-hardware theme) — no MCP budget was consumed.
- **Catalyst gaps:** Kurita Water's +15.06% has **no fresh catalyst found** in the sources checked; Yahoo/moomoo list its next print on 5 Nov (Q2).
- TAIEX level carries a 0.10pp source conflict (Yahoo -0.83% vs Investing.com -0.73%); Yahoo's figure is published.
- **Candidate trimming:** pool capped at 15 per direction per market as specified (JP 15/15, TW 15/15, HK 15/3, KR 15/5).
- The NOTABLE lines were topped up to 8 from beyond that cap where the capped pool had no 2-4% names to show; those extra lines are flagged inline.
- **Limit moves:** TW Syntec -9.97% is a genuine limit-down lock (2nd consecutive session).
- No KR limit move (HLB -17.69% is inside the KOSDAQ ±30% band and is a fundamental repricing, not a limit).
- TSE has no daily limit for large caps since Oct 2024, so Japan -10% prints are real.
- **Thin prints:** `HKEX:247` Tsim Sha Tsui Properties traded 1 share, so its -2.97% is indicative only. `KRX:008930`, `HKEX:326` and `HKEX:3774` carry no next-print date in the scanner.
- **KRX caveat honoured:** HLB is tagged as a fundamental move, not `KR_LIMIT_MOVE`; no combined_analysis/news tool was reachable, so catalyst attribution came from the local press instead.
- **Earnings calendar:** the scanner's `earnings_release_next_date` column is forward-looking only — it is used as a 'next print' date, never as a 'reported today' flag.
